JYOTI STRUCTURES : LENDERS BEGIN RELEASING RS 510.59 CR BANK GUARANTEE/LC FACILITY

• Lenders have started progressively releasing/disbursing bank guarantees and letters of credit under the NCLT-approved resolution plan
• Total BG/LC facility envisaged under the resolution plan is ₹510.59 Cr; release comes after a five-year delay
• Follows NCLAT order of 26 May 2026 for release/disbursal as per the NCLT-approved resolution plan
• Non-availability of these facilities had been a limitation on executing the company's order book
• Availability strengthens the operational platform and ability to execute the growing order book and pursue new opportunities in power transmission and infrastructure
Impact: Positive (eases the key execution constraint on the order book and supports bidding for new T&D work)

ELITECON : SECURES EXCLUSIVE ALL-INDIA RIGHTS FOR FOUR THAI FMCG BRANDS

• Exclusive Distribution Rights Agreement dated November 10, 2026 with Star Herb Pharma Company Limited, Thailand
• Covers PRIKKA, Fiberr, Star Cafe' and Starella brands across all States and Union Territories through general trade, modern trade, e-commerce, quick-commerce, HoReCa and institutional channels
• No fixed consideration or committed purchase value specified; supply terms to be agreed through separate purchase orders and trademark licence is royalty-free
• Initial term of one year, renewable for successive three-year periods with preferential renewal rights in favour of Elitecon
• Star Herb barred from selling into India directly, through other distributors or via cross-border e-commerce platforms; all Indian enquiries routed to Elitecon
Impact: Positive (adds packaged beverages and wellness portfolio to the FMCG business without brand-building capex, though no guaranteed revenue commitment)

Maintain near-term Trading Buy and 12-month Neutral; hike December 2026 Nifty target to 26,100 from 25,000

Easing Iran tensions, softer crude prices, lower bond yields and improving flows support a near-term market rally

Strong earnings momentum offers temporary support, but weak demand and limited earnings upgrades threaten sustainability

Expensive valuations, fiscal constraints and AI-related risks cloud medium-term outlook; Financials remain the preferred sector

UBS on Tata Steel ; Neutral TP Rs 220

Reported Q2FY27 consolidated EBITDA of Rs105bn (1%/6% above UBSe/consensus), up 18% YoY driven by strong realizations.

India production/sales were up 9%/8% YoY (up 7%/16% QoQ), supported by stable demand across market segments.

Netherlands production/sales were down 9%/16% YoY (impacted by shutdown of direct sheet plant) while UK deliveries were also down 33% YoY.

Though consolidated EBITDA/ton improved by ~Rs560 or 4% QoQ to Rs13,462, India EBITDA/ ton declined Rs1,370 or 7% QoQ to Rs17,790, as higher raw material costs were only
partly offset by lower opex/ton.

Netherlands EBITDA/ton improved to Rs6,085, aided by key plant restart in early August.

UK losses (at EBITDA level) increased sequentially from Rs3.4bn to Rs7.2bn due to lower volumes and narrower spreads.

UBS on Hindalco ; Buy, TP Rs 1325

Reported Q2FY27 EBITDA at Rs128bn (+8%/+15% UBSe/consensus), up 43%/ down 8% YoY/QoQ

Beat was primarily driven by higher aluminium realizations, as well as strong Novelis performance.

LME aluminium prices were up 23%/ down 10% YoY/QoQ for Q2FY27, while LME alumina prices were down 3% YoY but up 13% QoQ.

Novelis shipments were 1% below UBSe at 919kt, while adj EBITDA/ton was slightly above UBSe (US$550) at US$553 (+23%/-2% YoY/QoQ).

Aluminium upstream EBITDA improved 55%/down 5% YoY/QoQ to Rs70bn (+12% UBSe), driven by higher LME benchmark, elevated realization premium, and in-line cost of production (CoP). 

Copper EBITDA also surprised positively at Rs16.7bn (UBSe Rs10.2bn), as EBITDA/t expanded to US$1,509 (UBSe US$850)

UBS on Britannia ; Buy, TP cut to Rs 5800

Britannia's stock return depends on convergence of three cycles: Input costs (whether headwinds are behind, with scope for margin expansion), demand recovery (whether

volume growth trajectory stays resilient), and valuation (whether it is significantly below earning cycle peaks).

11% volume growth in H1 and still good outlook for volume growth, makes it a favourable context
Stock has corrected c20% YTD over inflation concerns, especially in packaging & fuel, and now trades at 12month forward PE of c39x (c15% below 5yr median), which makes the valuation cycle also quite appealing.
However, prospect of margin cycle turning favourable has got deferred to FY28.

Nonetheless, continued progress on incremental price increases, towards double-digit earnings growth, could act as a key catalyst for stock.

CITI on CG Power ; Buy, TP Rs 1100

CG Power has informed exchanges that the Hon'ble High Court has stayed closure notice issued by the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) for its Waluj manufacturing facility in Aurangabad, Maharashtra
Co had received closure notice on 3 Nov, citing alleged violations under the Water Act, 1974 and the Air  Act, 1981.

Historically, companies facing similar notices have either secured interim relief through the High Court, with the matter subsequently resolved in their favor, or undertaken the required remedial measures and secured regulatory approvals.

With the stay order in place, do not expect any near-term disruption to operations, particularly as the Waluj facility contributes only ~2.5% of annual revenue.

In addition, available capacity at the Nashik plant (currently operating at below 85% utilization), along with the recently announced expansion expected to be commissioned in 3-9 months, should provide further support against any potential operational disruption.

CLSA on MRF ; O-P, TP Rs 165238

2QFY27 Ebitda margin came in at 10.7%, contracting 73bps QoQ, led by a 95bps QoQ gross margin contraction due to an 8-9% QoQ increase in raw material basket price.

However, to combat this, tyre companies have already undertaken price increases of 13-15% in replacement segment in 1H, while cost reduction measures helped partially offset commodity cost inflation.

Also, OEM price revisions flow through with a one-quarter lag, implying full benefit of 2Q price hikes will be reflected in 3QFY27.

Consequently, expect profitability to improve from FY28CL as commodity prices soften on back of recent decline in crude prices & price hikes remain

JUBLPHARMA : JBI-802 PHASE 1 DATA SELECTED FOR ORAL PRESENTATION AT ASH 2026

• Preliminary Phase 1/2 data for JBI-802, a first-in-class oral dual LSD1/HDAC6 inhibitor, picked for oral presentation at the 68th ASH Annual Meeting (December 12-15, 2026)
• All 8 patients who started at 15 mg achieved over 50% platelet reduction or platelet normalization by Week 3, with median time to response of 15 days
• Platelet normalization maintained through 33, 44 and 46 weeks in 15 mg patients with more than 12 weeks of follow-up
• Seven of 11 patients with leukocytosis at 15 mg achieved a complete hematologic response
• No dose-limiting toxicities observed at 5, 7 or 15 mg; data cut-off June 30, 2026
• JBI-802 is being studied in essential thrombocythemia, polycythemia vera and MDS/MPN; Jubilant Therapeutics is a step-down subsidiary of Jubilant Pharmova
Impact: Positive (Early-stage clinical validation of the lead asset in thrombocytosis-predominant MPNs; ASH oral slot improves visibility, though data remain preliminary from a small patient set)

JEFFERIES ON INDIA EQUITY STRATEGY ; FPI INFLOWS SHOW SIGNS OF RECOVERY

• Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) flows have recently turned positive after persistent selling.

• Potential reversal in the AI trade could redirect foreign investments towards Indian equities.

• Equity tax relief, resilient domestic macroeconomic conditions and reasonable large-cap valuations could sustain FPI inflows.

• Light foreign investor positioning offers scope for additional buying.

• Jefferies identifies potential beneficiaries of renewed FPI inflows using three FPI ownership-focused stock screens.

JEFFERIES ON INDIA EQUITY STRATEGY ; PREFERS LARGE-CAPS ON POTENTIAL FPI RETURN

• Large-cap stocks could be the biggest beneficiaries of a revival in foreign portfolio investor (FPI) inflows.

• Large-cap valuations have become more reasonable, improving investment attractiveness.

• Higher liquidity and FPI ownership make large-caps the most direct beneficiaries of renewed foreign buying.

• TOP PICKS FOR FPI FLOW REVERSAL:

Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, UltraTech Cement, Max Healthcare, Varun Beverages, JSW Energy, DLF, Indian Hotels and Sona BLW Precision Forgings.

BOFA ON INDIA EQUITY STRATEGY ; POSITIVE ON NIFTY | YEAR-END TARGET 26,200

• Market risks are receding and corporate earnings are recovering; maintains a positive outlook on Indian equities.

• Most major uncertainties are now understood, supporting continued optimism on Nifty.

• El Niño and the upcoming Pay Commission remain key factors to monitor.

• PREFERS LARGE-CAPS over small-cap and mid-cap stocks.

MORGAN STANLEY ON GLOBAL AI SECTOR ; BUY THE DIP | AI INVESTMENT OPPORTUNITIES POST US MIDTERMS

• AI CAPEX GUIDANCE UNCHANGED: Maintains hyperscaler capex forecasts of $1.67 trillion in 2027 and $1.76 trillion in 2028.

• DATA CENTRE DELAYS: Expects around 20% of US data-centre projects scheduled for 2028 to shift into 2029, equivalent to 5 GW of capacity.

• 2027 OUTLOOK INTACT: Texas election results and new data-centre approval processes unlikely to disrupt projects already under construction.

• CAPACITY GROWTH: US data-centre capacity additions expected to decline 4% YoY in 2028 before surging 38% in 2029.

• GLOBAL SPILLOVER: Project delays in the US could redirect around 20 GW of potential data-centre development towards Asia and EMEA.

• POWER SHORTAGE: Morgan Stanley's AI model indicates over 30% power-capacity shortfall through 2028, supporting demand for existing operational data centres.

• AI EFFICIENCY: Meta targets 10x improvement in compute efficiency in 2027; TPU advancements could further improve AI training and inference economics.

• TOP HYPERSCALER PICKS: Overweight Amazon, Meta and Alphabet, supported by scale, capital access and AI infrastructure advantages.

• AI INFRASTRUCTURE PICKS: Favours Equinix and selected powered-shell providers amid infrastructure bottlenecks.

• DATA CENTRE RISKS: US permitting restrictions, higher development costs and slower project approvals could pressure 2028 infrastructure orders.

• KEY STRATEGY: Views the recent AI-stock correction as overdone; recommends selectively buying hyperscalers, infrastructure companies and AI software enablers.

• LONG-TERM VIEW: Believes project delays could extend the AI investment cycle rather than derail it, favouring well-capitalised technology leaders.

NVIDIA ESPIONAGE REPORTS COULD TRIGGER TOUGHER US CHIP EXPORT RESTRICTIONS

Raymond James warns that reports of alleged Chinese espionage targeting Nvidia ($NVDA ) could accelerate congressional support for the MATCH Act, which would tighten semiconductor and chipmaking equipment exports to China.

The legislation has bipartisan backing, with incoming Democratic congressional majorities potentially pushing for even stricter controls.

Additional restrictions could threaten the fragile US-China trade détente, particularly China's continued supply of rare earth minerals.

CITI DOWNGRADES US STOCKS AND TECH, TURNS BULLISH ON EUROPE

The bank warns that the Nasdaq could fall another 5% before positioning turns decisively bearish.

Meanwhile, European equities excluding the UK were upgraded to Overweight, benefiting from lower oil prices and reduced technology exposure.

Decision underscores challenges of implementing unilateral tariff actions in prepaid smartphone segment, where competitive intensity remains highest

• DEFENSIVE STOCKS: Consumer staples and healthcare rallied as falling bond yields encouraged investors to rotate away from AI-linked stocks.

• METALS: Maintains a positive outlook on industrial and precious metals.

• ELECTRIFICATION: High energy prices, electric vehicles, air conditioning and data-centre expansion support long-term electricity demand.

• EMERGING MARKETS: Earnings growth estimated at 65% in 2026 and 20% in 2027, outperforming developed markets.

• AI INVESTMENTS: Strong AI spending supports earnings, but elevated valuations and funding requirements pose risks.

• US FED: Inflation trends remain critical to future interest-rate decisions; financial conditions and tariff pressures are key monitorables.

• EQUITIES: Prefers quality companies with strong balance sheets, sustainable earnings and attractive valuations.

• COPPER: Sees upside potential from electrification, data centres and energy-security demand amid constrained mine supply.

• GOLD: Central bank demand remains robust, supporting the outlook.

• CRUDE OIL: Expects energy prices to moderate as supply-demand conditions normalise; Middle East tensions and colder weather remain upside risks.

• CREDIT MARKETS: Cautious on AI-linked technology debt and selected high-yield segments due to potential funding pressures and spread widening.

SHYAM METALICS : CRISIL REAFFIRMS AA+/STABLE AND A1+ RATINGS

• CRISIL reaffirmed long-term rating at CRISIL AA+/Stable and short-term rating at CRISIL A1+
• Rated bank debt enhanced to ₹4,500 Cr from ₹3,600 Cr; ₹50 Cr commercial paper programme reaffirmed at CRISIL A1+
• Rating rationale cites established steel market position, strong financial risk profile and healthy operating performance
• Multi-year capex for capacity expansion to be funded mainly through internal accruals and cash reserves, keeping debt metrics safe
• Expansion into flat steel, pig iron, stainless steel and aluminium foil continues; aggregate installed metal capacity at 16.93 MTPA
Impact: positive (higher rated debt limit gives funding headroom for brownfield capex while ratings stay reaffirmed)

MOREPEN : LAUNCHES FIRST U.S. PRESCRIPTION GENERIC DESLORATADINE TABLETS

• Desloratadine Tablets USP 5 mg launched in 100-count and 500-count packs for U.S. distribution
• Launch undertaken through wholly owned U.S. arm Morepen Bio Inc.
• Builds on long-standing Desloratadine API supply to the U.S. market, extending into finished dosage
• First ANDA filed with U.S. FDA for Sitagliptin Phosphate Tablets USP 25 mg, 50 mg and 100 mg; under regulatory review
• Company intends further U.S. Rx generic filings and may evaluate high-potency APIs and oncology
Impact: Positive (Moves Morepen up the value chain from API supplier into U.S. finished-dosage generics, adding a new revenue layer alongside CDMO)

DEEP IND , DOLPHIN OFFSHORE , JINDAL DRILLING , SEAMEC , ASIAN ENERGY; ONGC, RELIANCE & BP EXPLORE $1 BN OFFSHORE GAS INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT - ET 🟢🟢

• Major Proposal: ONGC, Reliance Industries and BP are exploring a common offshore infrastructure facility worth approximately $1 billion

• Project Location: Mahanadi Basin, targeting natural gas and condensate production from deepwater and ultra-deepwater fields

• Government Initiative: Proposal initiated by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

• Project Status: Currently at preliminary discussion stage; technical consultants expected to be appointed

• Shared Infrastructure: Companies could jointly utilise offshore facilities instead of developing separate infrastructure for individual discoveries

• Cost Savings: Common facilities aim to reduce development costs and improve operational efficiency

• Commercial Viability: Shared infrastructure could make smaller offshore gas discoveries economically viable

• Oil Ancillaries Opportunity: Potential future demand for offshore engineering, subsea equipment, pipelines, drilling support and marine infrastructure services

• Key Clarification: No final investment decision, EPC contract award or project execution timeline has been announced

Nuvama on Tata Steel ; Upgrade to Buy, TP 219

Inline stdlne EBITDA; +9.6% QoQ led by vols (+16%).

EBITDA/tn @INR 17.2k.

Mgmt guided INR 3.5k/$20 QoQ/tn +ve pricng for steel/coal in3Q; implying better profits in 3Q.
Netherlands EBITDA ++ amid higher steel prices & lower CoP (DSP restart).

UK losses widened due to lower vols; can breakeven in 4Q.
Raised FY27E/28E EBITDA by 2%/9% to factor higher prices & iron ore sales.

Kotak Inst Eqt on Tata Steel ; Upgrade to Add, TP Rs 200

TATA’s 2QFY27 operating performance was in line, with strong India earnings offsetting persistent weakness in Europe.

An increasing focus on downstream expansion and strategic sales of surplus iron ore should aid domestic margins in the medium term.

In Netherlands, unresolved regulatory resolutions continue to cloud visibility on decarbonization investments

Raise earnings estimates on higher domestic steel spreads

CLSA on Tata Steel ; O-P, TP Rs 225

2Q Ebitda (+14% QoQ/+18% YoY) was ahead of estimate on India and Netherlands profitability, while UK remained a drag

Expect earnings momentum to strengthen in 2H, supported by higher India volume and prices, improving Netherlands operations and the UK moving towards breakeven (guided by 4QFY27).

It expects India 3Q realisations to be up c.Rs3,500/t QoQ, partly offset by c.US$15/t higher coal costs.

Near-term growth will be supported by downstream mix improvement, higher iron ore sales and structural cost savings, before upstream capacity comes on stream.

JPM on Divis Labs ; OW, TP raised to Rs 12500

Strong 2QFY27, with revenue/EBITDA up 35%/76% YoY and beating consensus by 15%/33%, driven by custom synthesis (+54% YoY) on continued validation-batch supplies.

What lies ahead is conversion of validation into commercialization across three dedicated programs (one nearing commercialization; two progressing over next few quarters subject to customer qualification & regulatory clearance) & peptides scaling as Divi’s adds multi-tonne capacity via multiple 3,000-litre SPPS reactors and targets a top-three integrated global position in peptides

For context, largest player in peptides – WuXi Apptec – has >100KL peptide capacity & has targeted TIDES revenues of $2.5bn in CY26, underscoring size of the opportunity.

Against this backdrop, raise our FY27–29 earnings forecasts by 18-30%

GS on Divis Labs ; Buy, TP Rs 11700

2Q Revenue/EBITDA grew +35%/+76% yoy, significantly ahead of GS/street expectations (+21%/+38% vs GSe), primarily driven by Custom synthesis (CS), which grew 54% yoy (+34% vs GSe), while Generics also improved (+12% yoy, +4% vs GSe) on healthy volume growth, despite pricing pressure persisting in certain product categories.

EBITDA margin came in at 42.6% (+535bps vs GSe, +989bps yoy) driven by better mix (higher CS), backward integration benefits at Unit 3, & operating leverage.

Raise FY27-29E EPS by up to 17% to factor in Q2 beat

CITI on Siemens ; Neutral, TP Rs 3875

Q2 ahead of Citi estimates across revenue, EBITDA and PAT.

Orders rose 38% YoY to Rs62.3bn (with reported growth benefitting from price hikes), 4% ahead of Citie, & backlog increased 12% YoY to Rs470bn.

Revenue grew 17% YoY to Rs57.3bn, 5% ahead of Citie, with growth led by smart infra and mobility.

EBITDA margin recovered QoQ to 10.9% from 8.3%(adjusted for mobility one-off) in JuneQ26, albeit down c150bps YoY given continuing commodity and FX headwinds.
QoQ margin recovery in smart infra was a clear positive - believe this partly reflects price hike impact apart from operating leverage.

While mobility margins also recovered QoQ, mobility margins have historically been more volatile versus smart infra.

EBITDA at Rs6.3bn was 24% ahead of Citie.

Overall, robust orders and sequential EBITDA margin are encouraging though gross margins remain a monitorable - sustainability of EBITDA margin improvement would be key.

CITI on Hindalco ; Neutral, TP cut to Rs 1050

2Q consol EBITDA rose 42% yoy/ fell 8% qoq.

India upstream: Rs70bn vs. Rs73.9bn in 1Q, India downstream: Rs3.3bn vs. Rs3bn, Copper: Rs16.7bn vs. Rs9.2bn, Novelis:Rs48.6bn vs. Rs48.8bn.

India upstream EBITDA/t: $2,125 vs. $2,331 in 1Q, should decline (spot $3,050 vs. $3,227 in 1Q).

Key highlights: (1) net D/EBITDA 1.8x vs. 1.95x, (2) Novelis insurance recovery at $1.3bn ($900m to date) out of $1.8bn, (3) India 2Q COP up 5%, 3Q to rise by another ~5% (costs should decline in 4Q), (4) FY28 hedge position: 26% at $3,168/t.

Neutral, LME upside from spot likely limited (LME est CY27 $3,000, spot $3,070).

Upsides such as (1) Bay Minette profitability, (2) India expansion, (3) captive coal, are back ended.

CITI on Bharti Airtel ; Buy, TP Rs 2390

In a notable reversal, Bharti has reinstated its Rs299 recharge plan 3 months after withdrawing it in Aug'26.

While earlier plan offered 1.5 GB/day of data, relaunched version provides 1 GB/day.

Move reflects Bharti's response to competitive pressures, as peers did not follow its earlier tariff action, as well as elevated churn during 2Q.

Churn increased from 2.6% to 2.9% qoq, resulting in net subscriber additions slowing sharply qoq from +3.3m to +0.7m

Decision underscores challenges of implementing unilateral tariff actions in prepaid smartphone segment, where competitive intensity remains highest

It suggests that pricing discipline is difficult to sustain without broader industry participation.

Note that based on certain assumptions around Bharti's subscriber mix, had estimated the Aug'26 move could potentially benefit ARPU by c.Rs4/mth (EPS benefit of c.2%).

Bharti recently reported ARPU improvement from Rs264 to Rs271 in 2Q.

CLSA on Jubilant FoodWorks ; O-P, TP Rs 550

Reported 11.5% standalone sales growth in 2QFY27 and 4.1% Domino’s India LFL.

Ebitda grew 12.4% YoY, with margin expanding 16bps YoY to 19.8%, broadly in line with CLe

Management maintained its 5-7% LFL guidance for FY27 implying an acceleration in 2H.

Popeyes sustained strong momentum with 53% LFL and 122% revenue growth.

Innovation products are gaining traction, with contribution nearing double digits and superior margins.

Dominos turkey saw positive transaction growth.

Gross margin was in line with our expectations but 39bps better than consensus.

JPM on Jubilant FoodWorks ; Neutral, TP Rs 520

Q2 standalone EBITDA (+12.4% y/y) offered a marginal beat vs expectations.

Management is cautiously optimistic on the outlook (relying more on own initiatives vs broader industry momentum), targeting 5-7% LFL growth for FY27, with Q3 tracking to plan and delivery momentum remaining healthy

Dine-in/takeaway (growth turned positive but still soft), innovation (to support ticket size) and calibrated pricing should provide incremental growth levers.

On margins, despite commodity and operating-cost inflation, JUBI intends to deliver improvement through pricing, lower discounting, mix and cost efficiencies – reduction in losses on new formats is tracking ahead of expectations but stiff COGS/fuel and wage inflation have stalled margin progression for Domino's.

Popeyes posted 8% q/q revenue growth (11 new stores added) and remains a key medium-term growth engine, although expansion will stay disciplined until restaurant-level economics strengthen

Nomura on Gujarat Energy ; Buy, TP Rs 325

2Q misses high expectations, valuation attractive

CGD volumes may grow in double digits

Asset-light trading business generates healthy cash

GEL remains a deep value buy, but near-term earnings headwinds may persist

JPM on Gujarat Energy ;, Upgrade to OW, TP Rs 300

Stock (Gujarat Gas prior to the merger) is effectively down 39% YTD, underperforming the NIFTY c.34%
See two reasons:
1) concerns that elevated natural gas prices reduce both CGD and gas trading volumes (this has partially happened)
2) a reduction in multiples given the new gas trading business (c.40% of 2QFY27 EBITDA) can be more volatile

Stock is currently at less than 8x FY28E P/E (JPMe) & do not expect further valuation downside.

Propane has recently become cheaper than natural gas, which hurt GUJENERG’s volumes in 2Q.

While this drag may continue, natural gas prices should come off in medium term, it conflict in Middle East ends & large anticipated additions to global LNG capacity come through.

GS on Data Patterns ; Neutral TP Rs 4165

Q2FY27 performance was a miss across all key operating parameters, with revenue, EBITDA and PAT below our estimates by 10%, 47% and 52%, respectively.

On positive side, order inflows were strong at INR 9.3bn in Q2FY27, taking H1FY27 inflows to INR 10.5bn (nearly 3x YoY)

Confirmed order book stood at INR 17.4bn, with an additional INR 9.6bn of negotiated orders awaiting formalization, implying a combined order book and pipeline of INR 27bn.

Management maintained its FY27 guidance of 25% revenue growth and 35-40% EBITDA margin, implying a sharp H2FY27 execution ramp-up

At current market price, believe that risk-reward is balanced as sharp uptick in order accretion is offset by weak execution/margins in past two quarters.

GS on Azad Eng ; Buy, TP Rs 3125

Revenue increased 31% YoY & 11% QoQ to INR 1.91bn, 2% above estimate

Sequential improvement reflects continued revenue momentum amid ongoing capacity ramp-up.

EBITDA increased 38% YoY & 12% QoQ to INR 723mn, 4% above estimate

EBITDA margin expanded 177bps YoY and 56bps QoQ to 37.9%, 42bps above estimate.

Gross margin improved 738bps YoY and 120bps QoQ to 95.6%, 409bps above estimate, supported by a favorable movement in inventory-related costs.

Per management, revenue is likely to hit an annual rate of INR 13bn by FY28E, more than 2x the FY26 level.

Amagi reported a robust quarter.

GS on Amagi Media ; Buy, TP Rs 635

Earnings momentum has been solid, with elevated revenue growth, sustained higher operating leverage, & strong free cash conversion.

Additionally, company has been making investments in new AI products across the video value chain, including enabling clients to expand audience/revenue and improve cost structures, which believe should continue to increase Amagi's TAM and extend growth durability.

In its 2QFY27 earnings call, management was confident in sustaining c.20%+ constant Fx revenue growth over medium term, with 40%+ of incremental margins

See room for significant earnings compounding; forecast 50%

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
